feature: Interactive bird–seed pairs and actual opposing-pool score distributions
changes: The existing partner microscope in the main expedition and private field-study trials has a compact Explore bird–seed matches disclosure.

Illustrative beak and shell shapes and a calculated seed-access index respond to the actual selected potential parents. A short activity guides learners to hold one trait fixed and explore the opposing pool.

Every actual opposing member appears on a selectable nonlinear score curve, with previous-island origin and a dashed average-score line. Native selectors and keyboard points share the existing scoped parent choices.
The average of individual pair scores is compared with the score at the average partner trait; their difference exposes why a nonlinear rule needs the actual trait distribution.

Recorded and selected-calculation partner factors distinguish reciprocal weighting from the partners-off calculation. Inactive selection and reciprocal rules use factor 1. Empty averages remain undefined with an explicit access-zero breeding fallback.
Canonical matchup evidence is included in the existing journal and replayable JSON export. Main/private scopes and invalid saved-parent fallback use existing validated member choices.
Pair calculations generate no feeding events, births or random draws. Model assumptions, additional habitat/cost effects and the limits of coevolution claims remain explicit.

limits: These are calculated teaching scores and illustrative fictional trait shapes, not recorded feeding events or measured probabilities.
One selected pair does not set a parent’s reproductive share; the model averages across the actual opposing pool and uses the full two-parent lottery.
A nonlinear score at the mean trait can differ from the mean individual score. Two shifting traits alone do not establish reciprocal coevolution in nature.
